definition_zh: 维持；保养；供养；坚称；捍卫
definition_en: to keep something at the same level or in good condition, to support someone financially, or to state and defend a position
core_image: 一只手从下方托住重物，掌心始终不松，重物因此停在原处
scene: 长跑教练在赛道边提醒队员。He told them to maintain this pace and not to chase the runners ahead, so that the whole group kept an even rhythm of breathing.
sceneCN: 这里 maintain 是「维持、保持」（第 1 个义项：把速度维持在原有水平）；句意：他让队员保持这个配速，不要去追前面的人，好让整队保持均匀的呼吸节奏。图中可辨识物件：跑道、配速表、队员队列、教练手势；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 维持；保养；供养；坚称；捍卫

derivatives.zh: 维持；保养；维护费；生活费

senses.title: Keep at a level: hold a state steady
senses.titleCN: 维持水平：让状态保持不坠
senses.definition: to keep something at a particular level, rate, or state over time
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在一段时间内保持在特定水平、速度或状态
senses.example: The pilot maintained a steady altitude through the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在暴风雨中保持了稳定的高度。
senses.why: Latin manu tenere meant 'to hold with the hand'. The first sense is the plain physical image: a hand under a weight, neither lifting nor dropping it, so the level stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 manu tenere 意为“用手握住”。第一个义项就是最朴素的实体画面：一只手托着重物，既不举起也不放下，因此高度保持不变。

senses.title: Keep in good repair: service equipment
senses.definition: to keep a building, machine, or system in good working condition by regular checks and repairs
senses.definitionCN: 通过定期检查与修理，使建筑、机器或系统保持良好工作状态
senses.example: The crew maintains the bridge every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 养护队每年春天保养这座桥。
senses.why: A machine is held up by care: oil, parts, inspections. The hand now holds not a weight but a working order, and letting go means decay.
senses.whyCN: 机器靠照料才被“托住”：润滑油、零件、检查。手此时握住的不是重物，而是工作状态；一旦松手，就是衰败。

senses.title: Support financially: provide for someone
senses.definition: to provide money or resources for someone to live on
senses.definitionCN: 为某人提供生活所需的金钱或资源
senses.example: One salary was not enough to maintain a family of five.
senses.exampleCN: 一份工资不足以供养五口之家。
senses.why: To hold someone up can be economic: the hand supplies what keeps a household standing. The same verb that holds a level also holds people above poverty.
senses.whyCN: “托住某人”可以是经济上的：手提供让一个家庭站稳的东西。同一个表示“维持水平”的动词，也用来表示让人不至于陷入贫困。

senses.title: Assert as true: maintain that
senses.titleCN: 坚称：坚持认为某事为真
senses.definition: to state something firmly as true, especially when others doubt it
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地陈述某事为真，尤在他人怀疑时
senses.example: The company maintains that its product is safe.
senses.exampleCN: 公司坚称其产品是安全的。
senses.why: A claim is held the way a position is held: you keep it standing against pressure. The hand switches from supporting objects to supporting a proposition.
senses.whyCN: 一个主张被“握住”的方式，就像一个阵地被守住：你在压力下让它立着。手从托住物件转为托住一个命题。

senses.title: Defend a position: stand one's ground
senses.titleCN: 捍卫立场：守住自己的阵地
senses.definition: to defend or uphold an opinion, right, or position against opposition
senses.definitionCN: 面对反对仍捍卫或坚持某种意见、权利或立场
senses.example: She maintained her innocence throughout the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 整个审判期间她都坚持自己是无辜的。
senses.why: This is the military edge of the hand image: holding a line under attack. The assertion is not merely spoken but kept in place while others push against it.
senses.whyCN: 这是“手”的意象中带军事意味的一面：在攻击下守住一条线。主张不只是被说出，而是在别人推挤时仍被保持在原位。

senses.title: Keep records or accounts systematically
senses.titleCN: 维护记录：让账目持续完整
senses.definition: to keep records, accounts, or lists in an orderly and continuing way
senses.definitionCN: 以有序且持续的方式保存记录、账目或清单
senses.example: The lab maintains detailed logs of every experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室维护每次实验的详细日志。
senses.why: A record is a structure that collapses if nobody holds it: entries must be added, errors corrected, gaps filled. Maintaining is the regular hand that keeps the file from falling into disorder.
senses.whyCN: 记录是一种若无人托住就会塌的结构：要新增条目、修正错误、填补空缺。维护就是那只定期伸出的手，让档案不至于陷入混乱。

senses.title: Keep a system running: technical upkeep
senses.titleCN: 系统维护：让系统持续运行
senses.definition: to keep a network, website, or software system running and updated
senses.definitionCN: 使网络、网站或软件系统持续运行并及时更新
senses.example: Two engineers maintain the server around the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 两名工程师全天候维护服务器。
senses.why: Digital systems also fall if unsupported: patches, backups, monitoring. The verb extends from a physical machine to an invisible service that must be held online.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统若无人支持也会倒下：补丁、备份、监控。动词从实体机器延伸到必须被“托在线上”的无形服务。

senses.title: Keep health or weight stable
senses.definition: to keep one's body weight, health, or condition at a stable level
senses.definitionCN: 使体重、健康或身体状态保持在稳定水平
senses.example: He maintains his weight by walking to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠步行上班来保持体重。
senses.why: The body is the most intimate thing held steady. Maintaining weight is a daily counter-pressure against gain and loss, exactly the small continuous effort of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 身体是被维持得最切身的东西。保持体重，就是每天对增重与减重施加反向压力，正好对应那只手持续不断的小小用力。

senses.title: Usage boundary: formal upkeep, not mere keeping
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：正式的维护，不等于简单保留
senses.definition: a usage limit: maintain is more formal than keep, implies continuing effort, and maintain that is a formal way to report an assertion
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：maintain 比 keep 正式，含持续付出的意味；maintain that 是转述某人主张的正式说法
senses.example: She keeps a spare key; the building manager maintains the locks.
senses.exampleCN: 她留着一把备用钥匙；物业经理负责维护门锁。
senses.why: Keeping can be passive possession; maintaining requires active care. The word also reports a claim without endorsing it, so a news report can say 'the minister maintains' while leaving the truth open.
senses.whyCN: keep 可以只是被动地保有；maintain 则要求主动照料。这个词还能在不背书的情况下转述主张，因此新闻报道可以写“部长坚称”，同时把真假留空。

intro.en: Maintain comes from Latin manu tenere 'to hold with the hand', through Old French maintenir. The hand-to-support chain is unusually clear; only the ultimate Indo-European root of tenere is less certain.
intro.cn: maintain 经由古法语 maintenir 来自拉丁语 manu tenere“用手握住”。从“手”到“维持”的引申链异常清楚；只有 tenere 最深的印欧词源较不确定。

items.en: Latin manus meant 'hand'. Its ablative form manu appears in phrases describing holding, seizing, and handing over.
items.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为“手”。它的夺格形式 manu 出现在描述握住、抓取和交接的短语中。

items.en: Manu tenere meant literally 'to hold with the hand'. The phrase already implies keeping something from falling, which is the seed of every later sense.
items.cn: manu tenere 字面义就是“用手握住”。这个短语已经隐含“不让某物掉下去”，这正是后来所有义项的种子。

items.en: Old French maintenir meant 'to support, sustain, keep up; preserve'. French fused the Latin phrase into one verb and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语 maintenir 意为“支撑、维持、托住；保存”。法语把这个拉丁短语融合成一个动词，再传给英语。

items.en: English maintain is recorded in the 14c. with the senses 'to support, uphold, preserve' and soon also 'to assert, affirm'.
items.cn: 英语 maintain 在 14 世纪有记录，义为“支撑、维护、保存”，很快又出现“断言、坚称”义。

items.en: The chain runs from hand-hold to sustain, then to provide for, keep in repair, keep records, and finally hold a claim against doubt. Each step keeps the idea of not letting something fall.
items.cn: 引申链从“手持”到“支撑”，再到“供养”“保养”“维护记录”，最后到“在怀疑中守住一个主张”。每一步都保留“不让某物掉下去”的意思。

items.en: Modern English maintains bridges, servers, records, weight and arguments. Maintenance, with its shifted spelling, names the whole work of keeping things up.
items.cn: 现代英语 maintain 可以带桥梁、服务器、记录、体重和论点。拼写发生变化的 maintenance 则命名整套“让东西不倒”的工作。

note.en: The first group shares the maintain shape and the irregular noun maintenance; the second separates upkeep, endurance, protection, and assertion.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maintain 的词形与不规则名词 maintenance；第二组区分维护、持续支撑、保护和断言。

entries.definition: the work of keeping something in good condition, or the money needed to support it. Its spelling differs from maintain.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持良好状态的工作，或维持它所需的费用。它的拼写与 maintain 不同。

entries.definition: able to be kept up or defended. It is maintain plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可维持的；可维护的；可辩护的。它是 maintain 加 -able。

entries.definition: a person or thing that keeps something in working order. It is maintain plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持正常运转的人或物。它是 maintain 加 -er。

entries.definition: to continue to have or hold something in a particular state. It is more general and less formal than maintain.
entries.definitionCN: 继续保有某物或使其处于某种状态。它比 maintain 更一般、更不正式。

entries.definition: to keep something going over a long period, especially with resources or effort. It stresses endurance more than routine care.
entries.definitionCN: 在较长时期内让某物持续，尤指靠资源或努力。它比日常维护更强调持久承受。

entries.definition: to keep something in its original state and protect it from harm or decay. It focuses on preventing change.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持原状并防止受损或腐坏。它聚焦于阻止变化。

entries.definition: to state a fact or belief firmly. It overlaps maintain that, but carries no idea of upkeep.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地陈述事实或信念。它与 maintain that 重叠，但不含“维护、保养”的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin phrase manu tenere, the real collocations maintain order and maintain that, and the irregular noun maintenance.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁短语 manu tenere、真实搭配 maintain order 与 maintain that，以及不规则名词 maintenance。

normal.en: Manu tenere is 'to hold with the hand'; maintain is what a hand does when it refuses to let something drop.
normal.cn: manu tenere 就是“用手握住”；maintain 就是手不肯让东西掉下去时所做的动作。

normal.en: Maintain order means keeping a crowd or system from falling into disorder, one small correction at a time.
normal.cn: maintain order 指让一群人一个系统不陷入混乱，靠一次次小小的修正。

normal.en: Maintain equipment is routine care: oil, inspect, replace worn parts before they fail.
normal.cn: maintain equipment 是日常照料：上油、检查、在零件失效前更换。

normal.en: Maintain that ... reports a firm claim without saying whether the speaker agrees.
normal.cn: maintain that……转述一个坚定的主张，却不说明转述者是否同意。

normal.en: The noun is maintenance, not maintainance: the spelling shifted after the French noun.
normal.cn: 名词是 maintenance，不是 maintainance：拼写随法语名词发生了变化。

abstract.en: A hand under a falling object, applying just enough upward force to cancel gravity: maintain is continuous counter-pressure.
abstract.cn: 一只手托住下落的物体，施加刚好抵消重力的向上力：maintain 就是持续的反向压力。

abstract.en: A tightrope walker makes tiny corrections all the time; the walk looks still, but maintaining it is constant motion.
abstract.cn: 走钢丝的人一直在做微小修正；行走看似静止，维持它却是持续的运动。

abstract.en: A bridge is kept alive by paint nobody notices: maintenance is invisible until it stops.
abstract.cn: 一座桥靠没人注意的油漆活着：维护在停止之前都是看不见的。

examples.en: The team maintained its lead until the final minute.
examples.cn: 这支队伍把领先优势保持到最后一分钟。

examples.en: Regular checks maintain the machine far better than urgent repairs.
examples.cn: 定期检查保养机器，远胜于紧急抢修。

examples.en: The report maintains that the new policy has reduced waiting times.
examples.cn: 报告坚称新政策缩短了等待时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: “曼特恩”——曼特恩每天给机器上油，让它一直转下去 → maintain 维持、保养

root: 拉丁语 manu tenere“用手握住”＝manu（manus“手”的夺格）+ tenere“握持”；核心是“手不松开，东西就不倒”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of maintain, all from one hand: hold a level, service a machine, support a family, hold a claim, defend a line, keep records, keep a system online, keep the body steady, and finally the boundary between passive keeping and active upkeep.
sensesIntro.cn: maintain 的九个义项都出自同一只手：托住水平、保养机器、供养家庭、托住主张、守住防线、维护记录、让系统在线、让身体稳定，最后是“被动保有”与“主动维护”的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holds a weight from below and never lets go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从下方托住重物，始终不松开。

branches.en: LEVEL AND REPAIR: a hand keeps a height steady, or keeps a machine from decaying.
branches.cn: 水平与修缮：手让高度保持稳定，或让机器不至于衰败。

branches.en: PROVISION: holding someone up becomes paying for their living.
branches.cn: 供养：托住一个人变成支付他的生活所需。

branches.en: CLAIM AND DEFENCE: a proposition is held against doubt, and a position is held under attack.
branches.cn: 主张与辩护：在怀疑中托住一个命题，在攻击下守住一个立场。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: records and servers stay usable only while someone keeps holding them up.
branches.cn: 系统：记录与服务器只有在有人持续托住时才保持可用。

branches.en: BODY AND BOUNDARY: weight is kept steady, while maintain is distinguished from mere keeping by effort and formality.
branches.cn: 身体与边界：体重被保持稳定；同时 maintain 以“付出与正式度”区别于单纯的 keep。

intro.en: Maintain is a French verb that came from a Latin phrase, not a prefixed English word. English adds -ance, -able, -er and -ed; the noun maintenance shows a spelling shift.
intro.cn: maintain 是从拉丁短语来的法语动词，不是带前缀的英语词。英语加 -ance、-able、-er、-ed；名词 maintenance 显示了拼写变化。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on manus 'hand': manual, manuscript, manufacture and manumit all describe work, writing, making, or releasing by hand.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 manus“手”上：manual、manuscript、manufacture、manumit 都描述用手操作、书写、制造或释放。

items.meaning: the work of keeping something in good condition; the cost of support
items.meaningCN: 保养；维护；维持费用（-ance 构成行为或状态名词，拼写有变化）
items.exampleCN: 这栋建筑需要定期维护。

items.meaning: able to be kept up or defended
items.meaningCN: 可维持的；可维护的；可辩护的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The software is designed to be easily maintainable.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件的设计目标是易于维护。

items.meaning: a person or thing that keeps something in working order
items.meaningCN: 维持者；维护者（-er 表示执行该动作的人或物）
items.example: The maintainer of the archive checks it every month.
items.exampleCN: 档案的维护者每月检查一次。

items.meaningCN: 保养良好的；维持住的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 这座花园维护得很漂亮。

items.example: The hand is the image behind maintain and manual.
items.exampleCN: “手”是 maintain 与 manual 背后的意象。

items.example: The verb supplies the holding that maintain describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 maintain 所描述的“握住”。

items.example: French passed this hand form into English maintain.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个“手”的形式传给了英语的 maintain。

items.example: The same ending appears in retain, contain and sustain.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾见于 retain、contain 与 sustain。

items.structure: Latin tenens, present participle of tenere
items.meaning: one who holds land of another
items.example: The tenant holds the land without owning it.
items.exampleCN: 承租人持有土地但并不拥有它。

items.example: The museum retains the original frame.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆保留了原来的画框。

latinEntries.meaning: done with the hands; a handbook

latinEntries.meaningCN: 手稿；手写文稿（“用手写成的”）

latinEntries.meaning: to make goods, originally by hand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 制造；生产（原义“用手做成”）

latinEntries.meaning: to release a slave from ownership
latinEntries.meaningCN: 解放（奴隶）；原义“从手中放走”

definition_zh: 维护；保养；维持；维持费；生活费；扶养费；维修作业；维持性复述；维持期；装备维修保障
definition_en: the work of keeping equipment, buildings or systems in good condition; the act of keeping something in existence; or the money that supports a person
core_image: 一人一只手扶稳竖起的梯子，另一只手不停往齿轮上滴油
scene: 维修工扶着梯子给齿轮上油，日常的照料让设备继续运转。One hand steadies the ladder while the other keeps oiling the gears: this everyday care is maintenance.
sceneCN: 这里 maintenance 是「日常保养」（第 1 个义项：设备保养）；句意：一只手扶稳梯子，另一只手不停给齿轮上油，这种日常照料就是保养。图中可辨识物件：人字梯、油壶、齿轮、油迹、工具箱；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 维护；保养；维持；生活费；扶养费；维修作业

collocations.zh: 维持期（治疗或体重管理）

forms.label: 单数（不可数，指保养工作）
复数（罕用，指多笔扶养费或多类维护）

senses.title: Routine upkeep: keeping equipment in working order
senses.titleCN: 日常保养：让设备一直能转
senses.definition: the regular work of cleaning, checking, adjusting and repairing equipment so that it keeps working
senses.definitionCN: 为让设备持续运转而定期进行的清洁、检查、调整与修理工作
senses.example: The aircraft is in the hangar for routine maintenance.
senses.exampleCN: 这架飞机正在机库里做日常保养。
senses.why: Old French maintenir meant to hold with the hand, and maintenance first named the act of holding something up. Applied to machines, that holding up becomes regular servicing: the thing is held in working order.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 maintenir 意为「用手握住」，maintenance 最初指把东西撑住这一行为。用在机器上，「撑住」就变成了定期保养：让它一直保持在可用状态。

senses.title: Keeping something in existence
senses.titleCN: 维持：使某物继续存在下去
senses.definition: the act of keeping something in existence or at the same level, so that it does not decay or disappear
senses.definitionCN: 使某物继续存在或保持在同一水平、不至于衰败或消失的行为
senses.example: The maintenance of peace required constant negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 维持和平需要不断的谈判。
senses.why: The abstract sense comes straight from the literal one: to keep a thing in the hand is to keep it from falling away. What is held up here is a state, not a machine.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义直接从字面义来：把东西握在手里，就是不让它掉下去。这里被撑住的是某种状态，而不是机器。

senses.title: Money that supports a person: living costs, alimony
senses.titleCN: 生活费、扶养费：供养一个人的钱
senses.definition: money paid regularly to support a person's living costs, especially after a separation or divorce
senses.definitionCN: 定期支付以维持某人生活开支的钱，尤指分居或离婚之后的扶养费
senses.example: He pays monthly maintenance for his two children.
senses.exampleCN: 他每月为两个孩子支付扶养费。
senses.why: In law, maintenance was the support one person owed another. The image of holding someone up turns into money: what keeps a household standing is now paid in instalments.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，maintenance 指一方对另一方应付的供养。把人「撑住」的意象转成了钱：让一个家庭不倒下的东西，如今按月支付。

senses.title: Public upkeep: roads, bridges and structures kept in repair
senses.titleCN: 公共设施养护：道路桥梁的修补
senses.definition: the work of keeping roads, bridges, railways and public structures in good repair
senses.definitionCN: 使道路、桥梁、铁路与公共建筑保持良好状态的养护工作
senses.example: Highway maintenance closes one lane every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天公路养护都会封闭一条车道。
senses.why: The thing held up is now a public structure rather than a private machine. English uses maintenance for the state's duty to keep shared surfaces usable.
senses.whyCN: 这里被撑住的是公共建筑，而不是私人机器。英语用 maintenance 指国家维持公共设施可用的职责。

senses.title: System maintenance: keeping software and data healthy
senses.titleCN: 系统维护：让软件与数据保持正常
senses.definition: the work of keeping software, servers, networks or databases in working order, often by planned updates
senses.definitionCN: 通过计划性更新等手段让软件、服务器、网络或数据库保持正常工作
senses.example: Scheduled maintenance will take the site offline for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 计划内维护会让网站离线一小时。
senses.why: Digital systems decay in their own way: patches fall behind, disks fill, certificates expire. The old word for holding a machine up was simply carried over to the invisible machinery.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统有自己的老化方式：补丁落后、磁盘写满、证书过期。原先用于撑住机器的旧词，直接搬到了这套看不见的机器上。

senses.title: Maintenance rehearsal: holding an item in memory
senses.titleCN: 维持性复述：把信息按原样留在记忆里
senses.definition: in psychology, repetition that keeps an item in memory without connecting it to other knowledge or moving it into long-term storage
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指一种重复：只把信息留在记忆中，不与其它知识建立联系，也不转入长时记忆
senses.example: Repeating a phone number to yourself is maintenance rehearsal.
senses.exampleCN: 把电话号码反复默念，就是维持性复述。
senses.why: Here the thing held up is a memory trace. The word keeps its plain sense of holding, and the contrast is with elaborative rehearsal, which builds links instead of merely holding.
senses.whyCN: 这里被撑住的是一段记忆痕迹。词仍保留朴素的「撑住」义，与之相对的是精细复述——后者建立联系，而不只是撑住。

senses.title: Maintenance phase: holding a state instead of changing it
senses.titleCN: 维持期：不追求改变，只求稳住
senses.definition: a stage of treatment, weight control or training in which the present state is kept rather than improved
senses.definitionCN: 治疗、体重控制或训练中的一个阶段：保持现状而不继续改善
senses.example: After the diet, she entered a six-month maintenance phase.
senses.exampleCN: 节食结束后，她进入为期六个月的维持期。
senses.why: Medical language splits a course into an active phase and a holding phase. The second phase does exactly what the word says: it holds the gain already made.
senses.whyCN: 医学语言把疗程分为主动期与维持期。第二阶段做的正是字面所说的事：把已经取得的成果撑住。

senses.title: Equipment support in the military: keeping vehicles serviceable
senses.titleCN: 装备维修保障：让车辆武器随时可用
senses.definition: in military use, the logistics of keeping weapons, vehicles and equipment serviceable and supplied
senses.definitionCN: 军事用语中指使武器、车辆与装备保持可用并获得补给的勤务保障
senses.example: The unit's maintenance company repaired the trucks overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 该部队的维修连一夜之间修好了卡车。
senses.why: Armies turned upkeep into a named branch of logistics. The word covers repair, inspection, spare parts and recovery, all of it holding the force in a usable state.
senses.whyCN: 军队把保养变成后勤的一个专设分支。这个词涵盖修理、检查、备件与救援，全是把部队撑在可用状态。

intro.en: Maintenance came into English through Old French maintenance from the verb maintenir, which continues Latin manu tenere 'to hold with the hand'. That phrase is manus 'hand' plus tenere 'to hold'. The English noun first named the act of upholding something, then the money that upholds a household, and only later the servicing of machines. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: maintenance 经古法语 maintenance 进入英语，源自动词 maintenir，后者延续拉丁语 manu tenere「用手握住」，即 manus「手」加 tenere「握持」。英语名词最初指把东西撑住的行为，随后指撑起一个家庭的钱，最后才指机器的保养。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Maintenance becomes a standard engineering and computing term for planned upkeep, and maintenance-free enters product description.
items.cn: maintenance 成为工程与计算领域表示计划性保养的标准术语，maintenance-free 也进入产品说明。

items.en: Railways and factories give the word its modern weight: maintenance of rolling stock and machinery is a budgeted activity.
items.cn: 铁路与工厂赋予这个词现代的分量：机车与机械的维护成为要编预算的活动。

items.en: The legal sense 'support owed to a dependant' is recorded, turning upkeep into a regular payment.
items.cn: 「应付给受扶养人的生活费」这一法律义见于记载，把保养变成了定期付款。

items.en: English maintenance is recorded in the sense of upholding or defending something, borrowed from Old French.
items.cn: 英语 maintenance 见于记载，义为撑住或维护某物，借自古法语。

items.en: manu tenere 'to hold with the hand' is the source phrase; tenere also gives tenant, tenable, retain, contain and sustain.
items.cn: manu tenere「用手握住」是源头词组；tenere 还给出 tenant、tenable、retain、contain、sustain。

note.en: The first group separates the real family from words that only resemble it or are misspelled; the second compares near synonyms that each cover part of maintenance.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与只是形似或拼错的词分开；第二组比较近义词，它们各自覆盖 maintenance 的一部分。

entries.definition: a person or thing that holds a group together, or the rope that supports a ship's mainmast. It is main 'chief' plus stay, a nautical term, not manus plus tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 维系一个群体的主要人物或事物，或指支撑主桅的绳索。它是 main「主要的」加航海词 stay「支索」，而不是 manus 加 tenere。

entries.definition: to keep something in good condition, to keep it in existence, or to assert something firmly. It is the verb behind maintenance and keeps all three threads.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持良好状态、使某物继续存在，或坚定主张某事。它是 maintenance 背后的动词，三条语义线都保留着。

entries.definition: A common misspelling of maintenance, which follows the French stem mainten- rather than the English verb maintain. There is no such standard spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 这是 maintenance 的常见拼错形式；正确拼写沿用法语词干 mainten-，而不是英语动词 maintain 的词形。并不存在这一标准拼法。

entries.definition: the everyday care and cost of keeping property or equipment in condition. It leans toward the money and effort spent rather than the technical work.
entries.definitionCN: 让房产或设备保持状态的日常照料及其花费。它偏向所花的钱和精力，而不是技术性的维修工作。

entries.definition: the scheduled technical attention given to a machine, such as oil changes and inspections. It is the concrete task, where maintenance is the whole programme.
entries.definitionCN: 给机器定期做的技术性照料，如换油和检查。它是具体的一项活，而 maintenance 是整套安排。

entries.definition: the court-ordered payment to a former spouse. It is the legal name for one kind of maintenance, from Latin alimonia 'nourishment', not a general term for upkeep.
entries.definitionCN: 法院判决支付给前配偶的钱。它是 maintenance 中一种的法律名称，出自拉丁语 alimonia「滋养」，不是保养的统称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: manu tenere is 'hold with the hand'; maintenance is the act of holding something up so it does not fall.
normal.cn: manu tenere 是「用手握住」；maintenance 就是把东西撑住、不让它倒下的行为。

normal.en: The noun keeps the French stem mainten-, which is why it is spelled maintenance and not maintainance.
normal.cn: 这个名词保留了法语词干 mainten-，所以拼作 maintenance 而不是 maintainance。

normal.en: tenere, the 'hold' half, also gives tenant, tenable, retain, contain and sustain: every one of them is holding something.
normal.cn: 表示「握持」的 tenere 还给出 tenant、tenable、retain、contain、sustain，每一个都含有「握持」。

normal.en: The same noun covers a machine, a peace, a child and a data centre, because all of them can fall down if nobody holds them up.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既能指机器、和平、孩子，也能指数据中心，因为只要无人撑住，它们都会倒。

normal.en: maintenance-free is the exact negation: no holding up is needed.
normal.cn: maintenance-free 正是它的反义：不需要任何撑住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand under a leaning ladder: maintenance is that hand, whether the ladder is a bus, a marriage or a database.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手托住倾斜的梯子：maintenance 就是那只手，无论梯子是公交车、婚姻还是数据库。

abstract.en: See upkeep as a steady drip of small acts; stop dripping and the machine, the peace or the gain begins to fail.
abstract.cn: 把保养看成一滴一滴的小动作；一旦停止滴油，机器、和平或成果就开始衰败。

abstract.en: The word never means improvement: it means holding the present state, which is why a maintenance phase follows the active one.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不表示改善：它表示把现状撑住，所以主动期之后才有维持期。

examples.en: Poor maintenance is a more common cause of failure than worn parts.
examples.cn: 保养不善比零件磨损更常导致故障。

examples.en: The foundation pays maintenance to the families of injured workers.
examples.cn: 该基金会向受伤工人的家庭支付扶养费。

examples.en: Regular maintenance of the trails keeps hikers safe.
examples.cn: 定期维护步道能保障徒步者的安全。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门特嫩死」——门轴得常抹油，不然就卡死 → maintenance 维护、保养

root: 拉丁语 manu tenere「用手握住」＝manus「手」＋tenere「握持」，经古法语 maintenir、maintenance 进入英语。核心是「一直用手撑住，不让它倒下」：撑住机器是保养，撑住生活是扶养费，撑住状态是维持。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a hand holding something up. What changes is what is held: a machine, a peace, a household, a road, a server, a memory, a treatment result, or an army's vehicles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一只手把东西撑住。变化的只是撑住的是什么：机器、和平、家庭、道路、服务器、记忆、治疗成果，还是一支军队的车辆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand steadying a ladder while the other oils the gears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶稳梯子，另一只手给齿轮上油。

branches.en: HOLDING UP: the physical hand becomes routine servicing for a machine, and simple keeping for a state of affairs.
branches.cn: 撑住：有形的手变成对机器的定期保养，对事态则变成单纯的维持。

branches.en: MONEY AS SUPPORT: what holds a household up is paid regularly, and law names it maintenance.
branches.cn: 以钱撑住：撑起一个家庭的东西按月支付，法律称之为扶养费。

branches.en: SHARED AND DIGITAL SURFACES: roads and servers are held usable for everyone who depends on them.
branches.cn: 公共与数字设施：道路与服务器为所有依赖它们的人保持在可用状态。

branches.en: HOLDING A STATE: a memory trace or a treatment gain is kept exactly as it is, without further change.
branches.cn: 撑住状态：记忆痕迹或治疗成果被原样保持，不再进一步改变。

branches.en: HOLDING A FORCE: military logistics keeps vehicles and weapons serviceable so the unit can act.
branches.cn: 撑住武力：军事后勤让车辆与武器保持可用，使部队能够行动。

intro.en: Maintenance is Latin manu tenere 'to hold with the hand' plus the French noun ending -ance, from Latin -antia. The ending turns the act of holding into the name of that act.
intro.cn: maintenance 是拉丁语 manu tenere「用手握住」加法语名词词尾 -ance（出自拉丁 -antia）。这个词尾把「握持」这一动作变成该动作的名称。

latinIntro.en: The two Latin pieces are manus 'hand' and tenere 'to hold'. tenere supplies the stems ten- and -tain, visible in tenant, tenable, retain, contain, sustain and maintain.
latinIntro.cn: 两个拉丁成分是 manus「手」与 tenere「握持」。tenere 提供 ten- 与 -tain 词干，见于 tenant、tenable、retain、contain、sustain、maintain。

items.meaning: the act of keeping something up
items.meaningCN: 维持、保养的行为（-ance 构成动作名词）
items.example: Routine maintenance keeps the pumps running.
items.exampleCN: 日常保养让水泵持续运转。

items.meaning: to keep in condition, keep in being, or assert
items.example: They maintain the bridge every summer.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天维护这座桥。

items.meaning: able to be kept up or defended
items.example: The design is simple and easily maintainable.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计简单，易于维护。

items.meaning: the ease with which something can be kept in service
items.meaningCN: 可维护性；便于保养的程度
items.example: Engineers tested the maintainability of the new engine.
items.exampleCN: 工程师测试了新发动机的可维护性。

items.meaning: a person or tool that keeps something in order
items.meaningCN: 维护者；保养人员或工具
items.example: The software has only one active maintainer.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件只有一名在任维护者。

items.meaning: one who holds a rented property
items.meaningCN: 承租人；房客（字面「持有者」）
items.example: The tenant renewed the lease for a year.

items.meaning: able to be held or defended against objection
items.example: That argument is no longer tenable.
items.exampleCN: 那个论点已经站不住脚了。

items.meaning: to keep or hold on to something
items.meaningCN: 保留；保持（re- 表示向后）
items.example: The soil retains water after rain.

items.meaning: to hold inside, or to keep within limits
items.meaningCN: 容纳；控制住（con- 表示合在一起）
items.exampleCN: 这个盒子里装着旧信件。

items.meaning: to hold up from beneath, and so to keep going
items.meaningCN: 支撑；使持续（sus- 表示从下方）
items.example: The soil sustains a dense forest.
items.exampleCN: 这片土壤养着茂密的森林。

latinEntries.meaning: to hold with the hand, hence to keep up
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用手握住，因而引申为维持

latinEntries.meaning: forms an abstract noun of action, French -ance
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成动作抽象名词，法语作 -ance

definition_zh: 主要的；重大的；大调的；主修（科目）；少校；成年人
definition_en: greater in importance, size, or seriousness; of a musical scale built on a major third; as a noun, a main subject of study, a military rank, or a person of full legal age
core_image: 天平上更重的那一端：两边同时放上物件，major 是往下沉的一侧
scene: 开学前一周，她在选课系统里填表。She marked economics as her major and then signed the bottom of the form, which also declared that she was old enough to sign for herself.
sceneCN: 这里 major 是「主修科目」（第 5 个义项：大学里分量最重的学科）；句意：她把经济学标为主修，然后在表格底部签名，这一签也表明她已到了可以自己签字的年龄。图中可辨识物件：选课系统界面、经济学课程条目、签名栏与钢笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 主要的；重大的；大调的；成年的
主修科目；少校；成年人；大联盟
主修（常与 in 连用）

forms.label: 复数／三单（名词复数、动词三单，同形）

senses.title: The heavier side of a comparison: more important
senses.titleCN: 比较中更重的一侧：更重要
senses.definition: more important, more powerful, or more effective than other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类别中更重要、更有力量或更有效
senses.example: Tourism is a major source of income for the island.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是这个岛的主要收入来源。
senses.why: Latin maior is the comparative of magnus 'great'. The word begins as a weighing: two things are compared and one side is heavier. Importance is the first thing this comparison measures, before size or number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maior 是 magnus“大”的比较级。这个词的起点是一次称量：两样东西相比，有一侧更重。这个比较最先量的是重要性，然后才是尺寸或数量。

senses.title: Greater in scale or quantity
senses.definition: larger in size, number, or extent when measured against others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他事物相比，在尺寸、数量或范围上更大
senses.example: A major portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的一大部分用于工资。
senses.why: The same scale now reads quantity rather than rank. Because maior already carries 'more', careful English does not say 'very major': a big city can be a major city, but major itself never means merely big.
senses.whyCN: 同一架天平现在量的是数量而不是位次。由于 maior 本身已含“更多”，规范的英语不说 very major：大城市可以是 major city，但 major 本身从不只表示“尺寸大”。

senses.title: Serious enough to matter: medical and risk use
senses.titleCN: 重大到需要重视：医疗与风险用法
senses.definition: serious in effect or risk, especially of surgery, illness, damage, or change
senses.definitionCN: 在后果或风险上严重，尤用于手术、疾病、损害或变化
senses.example: The patient needs major surgery on his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人需要接受膝关节大手术。
senses.why: In medicine the comparison is between procedures that threaten the body and those that do not. A major operation is not simply bigger; it carries a higher risk, so the comparative becomes a judgement of severity.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，比较的两端是威胁身体的手术与不威胁身体的手术。大手术不只是“更大”，而是风险更高，因此比较级变成了一种严重程度的判断。

senses.title: Music: the scale a half-step greater
senses.definition: of a scale, key, or chord built on a major third, sounding brighter and more stable than the minor
senses.definitionCN: 指以大三级为基础的音阶、调或和弦，听感比小调明亮、稳定
senses.example: The piece moves from a minor key into a bright major key.
senses.exampleCN: 这首曲子从小调转入明亮的大调。
senses.why: Music borrowed the word in the 1690s because a major interval is a half-step 'greater' than the minor one. The comparison is now measured on the keyboard rather than on a scale of importance.
senses.whyCN: 音乐在 17 世纪 90 年代借用这个词，因为大三度比小三度“多”一个半音。此时比较是在键盘上量的，而不是在重要性的尺度上量的。

senses.title: University: the subject weighted most
senses.definition: the main subject a student specializes in, or to specialize in that subject
senses.definitionCN: 学生专攻的主修科目，或专攻该科目
senses.example: She majored in economics and minored in statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 她主修经济学，辅修统计学。
senses.why: A degree is a set of subjects, and one of them is weighted more heavily than the rest. The noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890 and the verb by 1910, both keeping the heavier side of the balance.
senses.whyCN: 一个学位由若干科目组成，其中一门的分量重于其余。名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，动词义记录于 1910 年，两者都保留了天平上更重的那一侧。

senses.title: Military rank: the senior officer
senses.definition: an officer rank above captain and below lieutenant colonel
senses.definitionCN: 高于上尉、低于中校的军官军衔
senses.example: The major briefed the company commanders before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 少校在黎明前向各连长做了简报。
senses.why: The rank came through French major, short for sergent-major, from Medieval Latin major 'chief officer'. In a body of officers one is marked as the senior one, so the comparative is used as a title.
senses.whyCN: 这个军衔经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）来自中世纪拉丁语 major“首席军官”。在一群军官中有一人被标为资历更高者，于是比较级被用作头衔。

senses.title: Legal adulthood: the older side of the line
senses.titleCN: 法定成年：年龄界线另一侧的人
senses.definition: a person who has reached the age of legal adulthood, or the state of being of full legal age
senses.definitionCN: 已达到法定成年年龄的人，或处于完全法定成年状态
senses.example: A minor cannot sign the contract; a major can.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年人不能签这份合同，成年人可以。
senses.why: Medieval Latin major also named 'an elder, an adult'. Law needs a line between those who can bind themselves and those who cannot, and major marks the person on the older side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 major 也指“年长者、成年人”。法律需要在能为自己负责与不能负责的人之间划一条线，major 标记的就是这条线年长一侧的人。

senses.title: The top tier: major leagues and the majors
senses.titleCN: 最高层级：大联盟与顶级行列
senses.definition: in sport and business, the highest level of competition or the largest organizations, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在体育与商业中，最高级别的赛事或最大的机构，常用复数
senses.example: He spent six seasons in the majors before returning to coach.
senses.exampleCN: 他在顶级联赛打了六个赛季，之后回去当教练。
senses.why: Major league is recorded in baseball by 1892. The comparison now runs between leagues rather than people: one circuit is the greater one, and 'the majors' became shorthand for the top tier in any field.
senses.whyCN: major league 在棒球中记录于 1892 年。此时比较发生在联盟之间而不是人之间：有一个联盟是“更大”的，于是 the majors 成了任何领域顶级行列的简称。

senses.title: Usage boundary: major is not simply big
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：major 不等于“尺寸大”
senses.definition: major describes importance or seriousness rather than physical size alone; it is not graded with very, and minor is its usual opposite
senses.definitionCN: major 描述重要性或严重性，而不只是物理尺寸；它不用 very 分级，其通常的反义词是 minor
senses.example: The storm caused major delays, though the airport itself is not very big.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成了严重延误，尽管机场本身并不大。
senses.why: Because maior is already a comparative, 'very major' is redundant in careful use. A major city is important, not necessarily large; a big city is large, not necessarily important. Major and minor split one scale into two sides.
senses.whyCN: 由于 maior 已是比较级，规范的用法中 very major 是冗余的。major city 是重要的城市，不一定面积大；big city 是面积大的城市，不一定重要。major 与 minor 把同一把尺子分成两侧。

intro.en: Major is the comparative form of the Latin word for 'great'. It entered English around 1300 as a word of rank, and later spread to quantity, music, universities, armies and leagues — always marking the heavier side of a comparison.
intro.cn: major 是拉丁语“大”的比较级形式。它约在 1300 年进入英语，最初表示位次高低，后来扩展到数量、音乐、大学、军队和联赛——始终标记比较中更重的一侧。

items.en: First recorded in English as majour, 'greater, more important or effective, leading, principal'. From c. 1300 it also named an elder or an adult.
items.cn: 最早以 majour 记录于英语，意为“更大的、更重要的或更有效的、领先的、主要的”。约 1300 年起也指年长者或成年人。

items.en: From Latin maior (earlier *magios), the irregular comparative of magnus 'large, great'. A comparative built on a suppletive stem, not on a regular -ior suffix added to magnus.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 maior（更早作 *magios），是 magnus“大”的不规则比较级。它是建立在异干互补词干上的比较级，并不是在 magnus 后加规则的 -ior。

items.en: magnus and maior are traced to PIE *meg- 'great', the same root behind magnify, magnitude and master. This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: magnus 与 maior 被追溯到原始印欧语 *meg-“大”，也是 magnify、magnitude、master 的词根。这一重构属于一般认为，而非确证。

items.en: The sense 'greater in quantity, number, or extent' is recorded from the 1590s, extending the comparison from rank to measurable scale.
items.cn: “数量、数目或范围更大”的义项记录于 16 世纪 90 年代，把比较从位次扩展到可测量的规模。

items.en: The military rank appears in the 1640s via French major, short for sergent-major. The musical sense follows in the 1690s, from the idea of an interval a half-step 'greater' than the minor.
items.cn: 军衔义在 17 世纪 40 年代经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）出现。音乐义随后在 17 世纪 90 年代出现，来自“比小调音程多半音”的观念。

items.en: The academic noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890, major league by 1892, and the verb 'to focus one's studies' by 1910 in American English.
items.cn: 学术名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，major league 记录于 1892 年，动词义“专注学业”记录于 1910 年，属美式英语。

note.en: The first group shares the maior / magnus line or looks close to it. The second group separates words for rank, importance, size and degree, which English often uses interchangeably and often should not.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maior／magnus 这条线，或词形接近。第二组区分位次、重要性、尺寸与程度——英语常把它们混用，而很多时候不该混用。

entries.definition: the larger number or part; also the age of legal adulthood. It is the noun built on maior, not a synonym of major.
entries.definitionCN: 多数、较大部分；也指法定成年年龄。它是建立在 maior 上的名词，不是 major 的同义词。

entries.definition: the elected head of a city. It came through French maire from Latin maior 'greater, chief', so it is a cousin, not a derivative of English major.
entries.definitionCN: 民选市长。它经法语 maire 来自拉丁语 maior“更大、首领”，因此是远亲，而不是英语 major 的派生词。

entries.definition: grand and impressive in appearance. It comes from majesty, from Latin maiestas, built on the same maior 'greater' stem.
entries.definitionCN: 外观宏伟、威严的。它来自 majesty，再上溯拉丁语 maiestas，同样建立在 maior“更大”的词干上。

entries.definition: largest or most important among several. It is close to major but usually points to one clear leader, as in the main reason.
entries.definitionCN: 在若干者中最大或最重要的。它接近 major，但通常指向一个明确的领头者，如 the main reason。

entries.definition: highest in rank or authority. It stresses position at the top of a hierarchy, while major stresses weight in a comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 位次或权力最高的。它强调层级顶端的位置，而 major 强调比较中的分量。

entries.definition: first in importance, especially of a reason, aim, or sum. It is more formal and narrower than major.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要的，尤用于理由、目标或款项。它比 major 更正式，适用范围更窄。

entries.definition: large or important enough to be noticed or to matter. It can measure degree where major measures rank.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或重要到值得注意、值得当回事。它可量程度，而 major 量位次。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maior is the comparative of magnus, and the same 'great' stem runs through majority, majesty, magnify, magnitude and master.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：maior 是 magnus 的比较级，同一条“大”词干贯穿 majority、majesty、magnify、magnitude、master。

normal.en: maior is a comparative, so major always implies 'than the other one'. A major road matters more than a minor road, not because it is wider.
normal.cn: maior 是比较级，所以 major 总隐含“比另一个更……”。主干道比次要道路重要，不是因为它更宽。

normal.en: magnus 'great' gives magnify, magnitude and magnate; maior gives major, majority and majesty. One family, two stems.
normal.cn: magnus“大”给出 magnify、magnitude、magnate；maior 给出 major、majority、majesty。同一个家族，两条词干。

normal.en: The academic major is the subject given the most weight in a degree, which is why the same word also means 'the important one'.
normal.cn: 大学的 major 是学位中分量最重的科目，这也是同一个词又表示“重要的那一个”的原因。

normal.en: A major in the army is the senior officer in a group, and a legal major is the older person across the age line: both are the 'greater' side.
normal.cn: 军队里的 major 是一群军官中资历更高者，法律上的 major 是年龄界线另一侧的年长者：两者都是“更大”的那一侧。

normal.en: Major league and the majors keep the comparison between leagues: the top circuit is the greater one.
normal.cn: major league 与 the majors 保留的是联盟之间的比较：顶级联盟就是“更大”的那一个。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with two pans. Whatever is placed in them, major names the pan that sinks: more weight, more rank, more risk, more volume.
abstract.cn: 想象一架两端有托盘的天平。无论放进去的是什么，major 指的都是下沉的那一盘：更多分量、更高位次、更大风险、更大体量。

abstract.en: The comparison can be held between cities, keys, subjects, officers or leagues; only the scale changes, never the gesture of weighing.
abstract.cn: 比较可以发生在城市、调式、学科、军官或联盟之间；变的只是尺子，称量这个动作从未改变。

abstract.en: Because one pan is already lower, there is no room to add 'very': the comparison is complete before the adjective is spoken.
abstract.cn: 因为有一盘已经更低，“very”就无处可加：比较在形容词出口之前就已经完成了。

examples.en: Lack of sleep was a major factor in the accident.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足是这起事故的一个主要因素。

examples.en: She majored in history and later became a curator.
examples.cn: 她主修历史，后来成了策展人。

examples.en: The symphony ends in a confident major key.
examples.cn: 这首交响曲在一个自信的大调上结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: “梅杰”——梅杰先生主修经济学，后来升为少校 → major 主要的、主修、少校

root: 拉丁语 maior“更大的”，是 magnus“大”的比较级，核心是“两者相比更重、更高的一侧”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of major, all one act of weighing: importance, scale, severity, a musical interval, a chosen subject, an officer's rank, legal age, the top league, and the boundary where the word stops meaning 'big'.
sensesIntro.cn: major 的九个义项都出自同一次称量：重要性、规模、严重程度、音程、主修科目、军衔、法定成年、顶级联盟，以及它不再表示“尺寸大”的用法边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things are weighed, and major names the heavier pan.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西被称量，major 指更重的那一盘。

branches.en: WEIGHT: importance and quantity are the same comparison read on two different scales.
branches.cn: 分量：重要性与数量是同一场比较在两把不同尺子上的读数。

branches.en: SEVERITY: in medicine the heavier side is the higher risk, so the comparison becomes a warning.
branches.cn: 严重性：在医学里更重的一侧就是更高风险，于是比较变成一种警示。

branches.en: INTERVAL: music measures the greater interval on the keyboard, a half-step above the minor.
branches.cn: 音程：音乐在键盘上量出更大的音程，比小调高一个半音。

branches.en: SELECTION: a chosen subject and a top league are both the item given the most weight in a set.
branches.cn: 选择：主修科目与顶级联盟都是在集合中被赋予最大分量的那一项。

branches.en: RANK, AGE AND BOUNDARY: a senior officer and an adult past the legal line are the greater side of a hierarchy, while the last branch marks the point where major stops meaning 'big'.
branches.cn: 位次、年龄与边界：资历更高的军官与越过法定年龄线的成年人是层级中更大的一侧；最后一条标出 major 不再表示“尺寸大”的分界。

intro.en: Major is not built with a living English prefix. Its Latin stem maior is already a comparative; English only adds noun and adverb suffixes to the finished word.
intro.cn: major 不是用活的英语前缀构成的。它的拉丁词干 maior 本身已是比较级；英语只是在成品词后加名词与副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family splits into two stems: magnus 'great' (magnify, magnitude) and its comparative maior 'greater' (major, majority, majesty). They are one root seen from two angles.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族分成两条词干：magnus“大”（magnify、magnitude）及其比较级 maior“更大”（major、majority、majesty）。它们是同一个词根的两个视角。

items.structure: Medieval Latin majoritas, from maior (greater) + -itas (noun of state)
items.meaning: the larger part of a group; the winning number of votes; the age of legal adulthood
items.meaningCN: 多数；多数票；法定成年（-ity 构成状态或性质名词）
items.example: The majority of members voted for the change.
items.exampleCN: 多数成员投票支持这项改变。

items.meaning: extremely, or in a major way (informal)
items.example: I am majorly late for the meeting.

items.meaning: a military officer ranked below a lieutenant general
items.example: A major-general took command of the division.
items.exampleCN: 一位少将接管了这个师。

items.structure: major + domo (from Latin major domus 'chief of the household')
items.meaning: the chief servant managing a large household
items.meaningCN: 大管家；总管（原义“家宅之首”）
items.example: The majordomo greeted the guests at the door.
items.exampleCN: 大管家在门口迎接客人。

items.example: The comparative is the direct source of major.
items.exampleCN: 这个比较级是 major 的直接来源。

items.example: The positive degree stands behind magnify and magnitude.
items.exampleCN: 这个原级支撑 magnify 与 magnitude。

items.example: The stem appears in major, majority and majesty.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 major、majority 与 majesty。

items.example: It forms majority, the greater part.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 majority，即较大部分。

items.meaning: a person of great wealth or power
items.example: A shipping magnate funded the library.
items.exampleCN: 一位航运巨头资助了这座图书馆。

latinEntries.meaning: to make something appear or become greater
greatness of size, importance, or brightness
latinEntries.meaningCN: 巨大；重要性；星等（大小或程度的量）

latinEntries.meaning: a person with control, skill, or authority
latinEntries.meaningCN: 主人；大师；硕士（原指“更甚者、首领”）
威严；陛下（王室尊称，原义“伟大”）

definition_zh: 多数；大多数；多数票；议会多数派；法定成年
definition_en: the larger part of a group, the winning margin in a vote, the larger bloc in a legislature, and the age at which a person becomes legally adult
core_image: 人群沿一条线站开，超过半数的人站到同一边，把另一边挡住
scene: 选举结果还没贴出，镇公所外的长椅上已经坐满了等候的人。The majority of the town had gathered outside the hall before the count was read.
sceneCN: 这里是「多数、大多数」（第 1 个义项：人数较多的那一部分）；句意为票数宣读之前，镇上大多数人已经聚在会堂外。

pos.zh: 多数；大多数；多数票；议会多数派；法定成年

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语比较级 maior 直接借入，义为「主要的；专业」
由 majority 加 -arian 构成，义为「多数主义的；多数主义者」
由 majoritarian 加 -ism 构成，义为「多数主义；多数统治论」

senses.title: The larger part of a group
senses.definition: the part of a group that is larger than the other parts
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中比其余部分更大的那一部分
senses.example: The majority of the students chose the morning class.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数学生选了上午的课。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin maior, the comparative of magnus, so its core idea is simply the bigger of two shares.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 maior，是 magnus 的比较级，所以核心念头就是两份当中更大的那一份。

senses.title: The winning margin in a vote
senses.definition: the difference in votes by which one candidate or side defeats the other
senses.definitionCN: 一个候选人或一方击败另一方时所领先的票数之差
senses.example: She won by a majority of sixty votes.
senses.exampleCN: 她以六十票的优势获胜。
senses.why: Counting turns larger shares into figures, and once the larger share decides a contest it becomes a margin of victory.
senses.whyCN: 计票把较大的份额换算成数字，而一旦较大的份额决出胜负，它就成了胜选的优势票数。

senses.title: The larger bloc in a legislature
senses.definition: the party or group that holds more seats than its opponents in a legislature
senses.definitionCN: 在议会中比对手占有更多席位的政党或团体
senses.example: The majority pushed the bill through both houses.
senses.exampleCN: 多数派推动这项议案在两院都获得通过。
senses.why: Where votes decide seats, the winning share hardens into a standing bloc, and the comparative idea becomes a body with power.
senses.whyCN: 在按票数分配席位的场合，获胜的份额凝固成一个常设阵营，比较的概念由此变成一个握有权力的团体。

senses.title: The age of legal adulthood
senses.definition: the age at which a person is legally treated as an adult
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在法律上被当作成年人的年龄
senses.example: In that country a person reaches the age of majority at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个国家，人到十八岁就达到法定成年年龄。
senses.why: A young person who has lived through the greater number of childhood years steps into full legal rights, so the same idea of the greater share marks the passage into adulthood.
senses.whyCN: 一个年轻人度过较多的童年岁月之后迈入完整的法律权利，同一个「较大份额」的概念便被用来标志成年。

intro.en: Majority is built from the Latin comparative maior, greater, and the noun ending -itas, and English first used it for superiority before it settled on numbers.
intro.cn: majority 由拉丁语比较级 maior（更大的）加名词词尾 -itas 构成；英语最初用它表示优越，之后才固定到数量上。

items.en: Magnus meant great or large, and its comparative maior meant greater.
items.cn: magnus 意为大的、伟大的，它的比较级 maior 意为更大的。

items.en: Maior, also written major, supplied the adjective for the larger of two shares.
items.cn: maior 也写作 major，用来指两份之中较大的那一份。

items.en: The abstract noun maioritas named the state of being greater, and French carried it onward as majorite.
items.cn: 抽象名词 maioritas 指「更大的状态」，法语又把它作为 majorite 继续传下去。

items.en: Early English majority meant superiority or precedence before it was applied to the greater number of votes or people.
items.cn: 早期的英语 majority 先表示优越、优先，之后才用于指较多的票数或人数。

items.en: Modern English extends the noun to election margins, parliamentary blocs and the legal age of adulthood.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词扩展到选举票差、议会多数派以及法定成年年龄。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin comparative maior and the root magnus; the near-meaning group gathers words for the greatest share and the winning side.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁比较级 maior 与词根 magnus 上的词；近义组收表示最大份额与获胜一方的词。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun that share the Latin comparative maior with majority.
entries.definitionCN: 与 majority 同出拉丁比较级 maior 的形容词与名词。

entries.definition: Favouring decisions by the majority, built from majority plus -arian.
entries.definitionCN: 主张由多数人作决定，由 majority 加 -arian 构成。

entries.definition: Size or extent, from the same magnus root but with a different ending.
entries.definitionCN: 大小、程度，同出 magnus 词根但词尾不同。

entries.definition: The greatest possible amount, from the superlative of magnus.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最大量，来自 magnus 的最高级。

entries.definition: The greatest number or part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物中数量或部分最大的。

entries.definition: The main or larger part of something, especially a group.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物、尤指人群的主要或较大部分。

entries.definition: The largest number of votes when no one reaches a majority.
entries.definitionCN: 无人过半时得票最多的票数；相对多数。

entries.definition: A superiority in number or weight.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或分量上的优势。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin comparative turned into a noun, and its branches all measure one thing against another: shares, votes, seats and years.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把拉丁比较级变成名词，它的各条分支都在拿一件事与另一件事相比：份额、票数、席位与年岁。

normal.en: Majority starts with major, the Latin comparative for greater, so the word names the bigger share before it names anything political.
normal.cn: majority 开头就是 major，即拉丁语中表示「更大的」比较级，所以这个词先指较大的份额，之后才带上政治色彩。

normal.en: The ending -ity turns an adjective into a state, so majority is literally the state of being greater.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 把形容词变成状态名词，所以 majority 字面上就是「更大的状态」。

normal.en: In elections a majority means more than half, while a plurality means only more than anyone else; the two words should not be swapped.
normal.cn: 在选举里 majority 指超过半数，而 plurality 只指比其他人多；这两个词不能互换。

normal.en: The age of majority is the birthday when the law stops calling a person a child.
normal.cn: 法定成年年龄就是法律不再把某个人叫作孩子的那一个生日。

normal.en: Majority leader is a fixed title in legislatures, which is why majority can name a bloc and not only a number.
normal.cn: 多数党领袖是议会里的固定头衔，这也是 majority 能指一个阵营而不只是数字的原因。

abstract.en: Half a room standing on one side of a line: the moment the line is crossed, a crowd becomes a majority.
abstract.cn: 半屋子人站到线的同一侧：跨过这条线的那一刻，一群人就成了多数。

abstract.en: A tally sheet at midnight turns a crowd into a number, and a number into a winner.
abstract.cn: 午夜的一张计票单把人群变成数字，又把数字变成胜者。

abstract.en: Turning eighteen changes nothing in the body, yet the law suddenly calls the same person an adult.
abstract.cn: 满十八岁身体没有变化，法律却突然把同一个人叫作成年人。

examples.en: The majority of the students chose the morning class.
examples.cn: 大多数学生选了上午的课。

examples.en: She won by a majority of sixty votes.
examples.cn: 她以六十票的优势获胜。

examples.en: A two-thirds majority is required to change the constitution.
examples.cn: 修改宪法需要三分之二的多数票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马脚瑞梯」——多数人一起扶着一架马脚梯往上爬；记住 majority 是多数。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）→ 比较级 maior（更大的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 maioritas（更大状态）→ 法语 majorite → 英语 majority；同族词多与「更大、主要」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the larger share of a group; the same comparison then yields a winning vote margin, a standing bloc in a legislature, and the legal age of adulthood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一个群体里较大的那一份；同一个比较关系随后生出选举的胜选票差、议会中的常设阵营，以及法定成年年龄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn across a crowd, with more than half the people standing on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中间画一条线，超过半数的人站在同一边。

branches.en: a crowd outnumbering everyone else in the square
branches.cn: 广场上人数压过其他所有人的一群

branches.en: a count that decides who takes the seat
branches.cn: 决定谁取得席位的票数统计

branches.en: the winning side sitting together in the chamber
branches.cn: 在议事厅里坐在一起的获胜一方

branches.en: a birthday that marks legal adulthood
branches.cn: 标志法定成年的生日

branches.en: one word for the larger part and for being old enough
branches.cn: 同一个词既指较大的部分，也指年纪够大

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin comparative maior, the noun ending -itas, and a family of English forms built on both.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁比较级 maior、名词词尾 -itas，以及建立在这两者之上的一组英语形式共同承载。

latinIntro.en: Latin is the direct source here: magnus gave the comparative maior, and maioritas gave the abstract noun behind majority.
latinIntro.cn: 这里拉丁语是直接来源：magnus 给出比较级 maior，maioritas 则给出 majority 背后的抽象名词。

items.meaning: greater; main; a field of study
based on rule by the majority

latinEntries.meaning: the state of being greater; a larger part
latinEntries.meaningCN: 更大的状态；较大的部分

definition_zh: 做；制造；使得；作出；赚得；品牌
definition_en: to produce or create something, to cause something to happen or be, to carry out an action, to earn money, or, as a noun, the brand of a product
core_image: 一双手把散落的材料按在一起，桌上慢慢出现一个成形的东西
scene: 厨房里灯还亮着，面粉撒在案板上，孩子踮着脚看大人揉面。She made the dough before sunrise and left it covered by the window.
sceneCN: 这里是「做、制作」（第 1 个义项：把材料做成东西）；句意为她在日出前和好面团，盖上布放在窗边。

derivatives.zh: 由 make 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「制作者；制造商」
由 make 加 -ing 构成名词，义为「制作；形成过程」
由前缀 re-（再次）加 make 构成，义为「重做；翻拍」

senses.title: To produce or create something
senses.definition: to produce, build or create something out of materials or parts
senses.definitionCN: 用材料或零件做出、建造或创造某物
senses.example: She made a small wooden box for her letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她给信件做了一个小木盒。
senses.why: Old English macian meant to build or fashion, so the first sense is a hand shaping raw material into an object.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 macian 意为建造、塑形，所以第一个义项是手把原料塑成物件。

senses.title: To cause someone or something to be or do something
senses.definition: to cause a person or thing to enter a state or to perform an action
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物进入某种状态，或去做某事
senses.example: The news made everyone quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让所有人都安静下来。
senses.why: Once a hand can shape clay, the same verb is stretched to shaping events: what you do makes a result happen.
senses.whyCN: 既然手能塑造黏土，同一个动词就被延伸到塑造事件：你所做的使某个结果发生。

senses.title: To perform an action
senses.definition: to perform an action, especially one that is named by a noun, such as make a decision or make an effort
senses.definitionCN: 执行某个动作，尤其是由名词命名的动作，如作出决定、付出努力
senses.example: They made a careful decision before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前他们作了慎重的决定。
senses.why: English often pairs a light verb with an action noun, and make is the light verb that turns the noun into something actually done.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把轻动词与动作名词搭配，make 正是那个把名词变成真正做出来的事的轻动词。

senses.title: To earn or gain money
senses.definition: to earn money or gain a profit from work, trade or an investment
senses.definitionCN: 通过工作、买卖或投资挣到钱或获得利润
senses.example: The stall made a small profit on its first day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个摊子在开张头一天赚了一点钱。
senses.why: Producing goods that sell turns the verb for making objects into the verb for making money.
senses.whyCN: 把做出来的东西卖出去，就使「制造物件」的动词变成「赚到钱」的动词。

senses.title: The brand of a manufactured product
senses.definition: the brand or particular type under which a product is manufactured and sold
senses.definitionCN: 产品被制造和销售时所标的品牌或特定型号
senses.example: The two cars are the same model but a different make.
senses.exampleCN: 这两辆车是同一款，但品牌不同。
senses.why: A workshop name marked what it turned out, and that mark became the noun for the brand itself.
senses.whyCN: 作坊的名字标示它做出来的东西，这个标记后来就成了指品牌本身的名词。

intro.en: Make is a West Germanic verb for building that widened into causing, performing, earning and the name of a brand.
intro.cn: make 是西日耳曼语中表示建造的动词，后来词义扩展到致使、执行、赚钱以及品牌的名称。

items.en: macian meant to make, build or form, and it was one of the commonest verbs in the language.
items.cn: macian 意为制作、建造、塑形，是当时最常用的动词之一。

items.en: The reconstructed form *makōjanan meant to fashion or put together and is generally taken to be shared with other Germanic verbs of the same meaning.
items.cn: 重构形式 *makōjanan 意为塑形、拼合，一般认为它与其他日耳曼语中同义的动词同出一源。

items.en: macian became maken, and the meaning widened from building to any kind of doing.
items.cn: macian 演变为 maken，词义从建造扩大到各种「做」。

items.en: The pattern make someone do something became ordinary, and so did make in the sense of earning a living.
items.cn: 「让某人做某事」的句式和「谋生、挣钱」的用法在这时都变得平常。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb in hundreds of phrases and adds the noun make for the brand of a product.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个动词留在大量短语里，并添上名词用法，指产品的品牌。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built directly on make; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for bringing something into existence.
note.cn: 形近组收直接建立在 make 上的形式；近义组收表示使某物产生的动词。

entries.definition: A person or company that makes something.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的人或公司。

entries.definition: The act or process of producing something.
entries.definitionCN: 生产某物的动作或过程。

entries.definition: To make something again, or a new version of an old work.
entries.definitionCN: 重做某物，或旧作品的新版本。

entries.definition: Cosmetics, or the way parts are put together.
entries.definitionCN: 化妆品，或各部分的组成方式。

entries.definition: To bring something new into existence.
entries.definitionCN: 使新事物产生。

entries.definition: To make goods in large amounts, especially for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 大量制造商品，尤指供出售。

entries.definition: To make goods in a factory using machines.
entries.definitionCN: 在工厂里用机器制造商品。

entries.definition: To put parts together to form a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分组合成结构。

normalIntro.en: The word is a common Germanic verb for shaping material, and its uses spread from the workshop to causes, actions, wages and brands.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示塑造材料的常用动词，用法从作坊扩散到原因、行动、收入和品牌。

normal.en: Make is the everyday verb for turning material into an object, just as macian was in Old English.
normal.cn: make 是把材料变成物件的日常动词，古英语里的 macian 也是如此。

normal.en: Maker adds -er to make, so the person who makes is simply the verb plus a doer ending.
normal.cn: maker 在 make 后加 -er，所以「制作者」不过是动词加上表示做事者的词尾。

normal.en: The pattern make him wait is a shortcut: instead of doing the action, you cause someone else to do it.
normal.cn: 「让他等」这种句式是一种捷径：你不亲自做，而是使别人去做。

normal.en: Make a decision sounds strange in some languages, but English uses make as a light verb for actions named by nouns.
normal.cn: 「作出决定」在某些语言里说法不同，但英语把 make 当作轻动词，与名词命名的动作搭配。

normal.en: The noun make for a car brand comes from the workshop mark, not from the act of building.
normal.cn: 指汽车品牌的名词 make 来自作坊的标记，而不是来自建造这个动作。

abstract.en: Flour, water and a pair of hands: the table is empty, and then there is dough.
abstract.cn: 面粉、水和一双手：案板先是空的，然后就有了面团。

abstract.en: One sentence can push another person across a room without touching them, and English calls that making.
abstract.cn: 一句话不碰到任何人，就能把别人推得满屋走动，英语把这种作用叫作 make。

abstract.en: A name stamped on a car door outlives the hands that built it, and that name is the make.
abstract.cn: 印在车门上的名字比造它的那双手活得更久，那个名字就是 make。

examples.en: She made a small wooden box for her letters.
examples.cn: 她给信件做了一个小木盒。

examples.en: The news made everyone quiet.
examples.cn: 这个消息让所有人都安静下来。

examples.en: The two cars are the same model but a different make.
examples.cn: 这两辆车是同一款，但品牌不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克」——麦克风递到谁手里，谁就得当场做点什么；记住 make 是做。

root: 古英语 macian（制作、建造）源自西日耳曼语，一般认为与重构形式 *makōjanan 同源；同族词多与「做、制成、制作者」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the hand shaping material into an object; the word then extends to causing results, performing actions, earning money, and naming a brand.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是手把材料塑成物件；词义随后扩展到使结果发生、执行动作、挣得收入，以及给品牌命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pressing loose material together until a shaped object appears on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把松散的材料按在一起，桌上渐渐出现一个成形的物件。

branches.en: flour and water turning into dough under a pair of hands
branches.cn: 面粉与水在一双手下变成面团

branches.en: a single sentence that pushes someone into action
branches.cn: 一句话把别人推入行动

branches.en: a decision written down before the meeting begins
branches.cn: 会前就写好的决定

branches.en: coins counted at the end of a market day
branches.cn: 集市散场后数起的硬币

branches.en: two cars of the same make parked side by side
branches.cn: 两辆同品牌的车并排停着

intro.en: The word rests on one Old English verb, its irregular past form, and a set of suffixes and compounds that keep the idea of producing.
intro.cn: 这个词依靠一个古英语动词、它不规则的变化形式，以及一组保留「制作」含义的后缀与复合词支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its recorded relatives are Germanic, including the reconstructed *makōjanan.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它的有据亲属属于日耳曼语，包括重构形式 *makōjanan。

items.meaning: to make again; a new version

definition_zh: 男性的；雄性的；男子；雄性动物；阳端的
definition_en: of the sex that does not give birth; an adult man or a male animal; also the masculine or technical male side of something
core_image: 一只公鸡站在栅栏上，冠子在晨光里通红，尾羽垂下成一道弧
scene: 农场清晨，栅栏边的公鸡昂着头，羽毛在斜光里发亮。The male bird crowed at the fence while the hens stayed in the shade.
sceneCN: 这里是「雄性的、公的」（第 2 个义项：动物中的雄性）；句意为栅栏边的公鸡打鸣时，母鸡都待在阴凉处。

derivatives.zh: 与 male 同出拉丁语 masculus，义为「有男子气质的；男性的」
由 masculine 加 -ity 构成，义为「男子气概；男性特质」
由 male 加 -ness 构成，义为「男性特质；雄性特征」

senses.title: An adult man
senses.definition: a person of the sex that does not give birth, especially an adult man
senses.definitionCN: 不生育的一性的人，尤指成年男子
senses.example: Two male nurses joined the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 两名男护士加入了夜班。
senses.why: Latin mas named the male of any species, and English kept the noun for men while the adjective spread to animals and machines.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mas 指任何物种中的雄性，英语保留其名词用法指男子，而形容词用法则扩展到动物与机械。

senses.title: The sex of animals and plants
senses.definition: belonging to the sex of animals or plants that produces sperm
senses.definitionCN: 属于产生精子的那一性，用于动物或植物
senses.example: The male flowers open before the female ones.
senses.exampleCN: 雄花比雌花开得早。
senses.why: Because the same biological distinction runs through plants as through animals, the word serves as a label for any organism of that sex.
senses.whyCN: 同一种生理区分在植物和动物身上一样成立，所以这个词可以用来标注任何属于那一性的生物。

senses.title: Having qualities thought typical of men
senses.titleCN: 男子气概的；男性特有的
senses.definition: having qualities that are traditionally associated with men, such as strength or a deep voice
senses.definitionCN: 具有传统上与男子相联系的特质，如力量或低沉的嗓音
senses.example: His manner was calm but unmistakably male.
senses.exampleCN: 他的举止沉静，却带着不容错认的男子气。
senses.why: A word for a biological class easily slides into a word for the behaviour expected of that class.
senses.whyCN: 一个标示生理类别的词，很容易滑向标示该类别的行为举止。

senses.title: The positive side of a connector
senses.definition: describing a plug, connector or fitting designed to enter its matching part
senses.definitionCN: 指设计成插入配对部件的插头、接头或配件
senses.example: The cable has a male plug at one end and a female one at the other.
senses.exampleCN: 这根线缆一端是阳插头，另一端是阴插头。
senses.why: Engineering borrowed the biological contrast of two mating parts and kept male for the part that fits inside.
senses.whyCN: 工程领域借用了两个配对部件的生理对立，用 male 指插进去的那一方。

intro.en: Male goes back to the Latin noun mas, whose stem mar- and diminutive masculus passed through Old French before English shortened it.
intro.cn: male 可追溯到拉丁语名词 mas，其词干 mar- 与指小形式 masculus 经古法语传入，再由英语缩略成形。

items.en: Mas meant a male person or animal, and its genitive stem was maris.
items.cn: mas 指男性的人或雄性动物，其属格词干为 maris。

items.en: Masculus was a diminutive of mas and meant male or masculine; it is the source of the English word masculine.
items.cn: masculus 是 mas 的指小形式，意为雄性的、男性的；英语 masculine 即出自它。

items.en: Old French wrote the word as masle or malle, and the l in those forms shaped the English spelling.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 masle 或 malle，正是这些形式里的 l 决定了英语的拼写。

items.en: Middle English male worked as both noun and adjective, and the adjective widened from people to animals and plants.
items.cn: 中古英语的 male 兼作名词与形容词，形容词用法又从人扩展到动物与植物。

items.en: Modern English adds the technical sense of a male plug and keeps the noun for men and male animals.
items.cn: 现代英语添上「阳插头」的技术义，并保留指男子与雄性动物的名词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin stem and one misleading look-alike; the near-meaning group gathers words for men and manly character.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词与一个容易误认的形近词；近义组收指男子与男子气质的词。

entries.definition: Having qualities traditionally associated with men, from Latin masculus.
entries.definitionCN: 具有传统男性特质，源自拉丁语 masculus。

entries.definition: The quality or state of being masculine.
entries.definitionCN: 男子气概；男性特质。

entries.definition: The other biological sex; the resemblance to male is only in spelling, since it comes from Latin femella.
entries.definitionCN: 另一生理性别；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自拉丁语 femella。

entries.definition: Having the qualities expected of a man, built on man rather than on male.
entries.definitionCN: 具有人们期待的男子品质，由 man 而非 male 构成。

entries.definition: An adult male human being.
entries.definitionCN: 成年男性。

entries.definition: A man of good manners and social standing.
entries.definitionCN: 有礼貌、有身份的男士。

entries.definition: A boy or young man, used chiefly in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 男孩或年轻男子，主要用于英式英语。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin noun for a male, reshaped by French spelling, and its family all points back to one biological contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中指雄性的名词，经法语拼写改造而定形，它的同族词都指向同一种生理对立。

normal.en: Latin mas, genitive maris, named a male, and masculus was its diminutive adjective.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mas 的属格是 maris，指雄性，而 masculus 是它的指小形容词。

normal.en: The l in male appeared in Old French forms such as masle, so the spelling changed while the meaning stayed.
normal.cn: male 里的 l 出现在 masle 这类古法语形式中，拼写变了，含义却没有变。

normal.en: Masculine and masculinity share the same Latin stem, which is why they all point back to mas.
normal.cn: masculine 与 masculinity 共用同一个拉丁词干，所以它们都回指 mas。

normal.en: Female looks like male plus fe, but it comes from Latin femella; the similarity is only in spelling, not in origin.
normal.cn: female 看起来像 male 前加 fe，其实它来自拉丁语 femella；相似只在拼写，不在词源。

normal.en: Technical writing uses male for the plug that goes inside, a direct borrowing of the biological contrast.
normal.cn: 技术写作里用 male 指插进去的那一端，这是直接借用生理上的对立。

abstract.en: A rooster on a fence post needs no adjective to announce its sex, yet English still labels it male.
abstract.cn: 站在栅栏桩上的公鸡不必用形容词宣告性别，英语仍要给它贴上 male 的标签。

abstract.en: Two identical plugs, one wider by a millimetre: the narrower one is called male because it fits in.
abstract.cn: 两个几乎一样的插头，一个宽了一毫米：较窄的那个因为插得进去而被叫作 male。

abstract.en: A deep voice and a firm handshake are read as male long before anyone checks a birth certificate.
abstract.cn: 低沉的嗓音与有力的握手，在任何人查看出生证明之前就先被读成男性。

examples.en: Two male nurses joined the night shift.
examples.cn: 两名男护士加入了夜班。

examples.en: The male flowers open before the female ones.
examples.cn: 雄花比雌花开得早。

examples.en: The cable has a male plug at one end.
examples.cn: 这根线缆一端是阳插头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买哦」——扛重活的多是男子，买东西的也多是他们；记住 male 是男性。

root: 拉丁语 mas（雄性，属格 maris）的指小形式 masculus 经古法语 masle 进入英语；同族词多与「男性、男子气」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the biological male sex; from there the word names an adult man, then a quality of behaviour, and finally the part of a connector that fits inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是生理上的雄性；词义由此指成年男子，再指一种行为气质，最后指连接件中插进去的那一端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rooster on a fence rail, chest out, tail feathers hanging in a single curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只公鸡站在栅栏横木上，挺着胸，尾羽垂成一道弧。

branches.en: a man standing at the front of a crowded room
branches.cn: 站在挤满人的房间最前面的男子

branches.en: a rooster crowing before daylight
branches.cn: 天没亮就开始打鸣的公鸡

branches.en: a voice and a stride read as masculine
branches.cn: 被听成男子气概的嗓音与步态

branches.en: a plug shaped to fit only one socket
branches.cn: 只有一种插座能插进去的插头

branches.en: one word covering men and male animals
branches.cn: 同一个词同时涵盖男子与雄性动物

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for a male, its diminutive adjective, the French reshaping, and English endings that name the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词依靠拉丁语中指雄性的名词、它的指小形容词、法语的改写，以及命名这种性质的英语词尾支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the whole line here: mas gave masculus, and masculus reached English through French before male was shortened.
latinIntro.cn: 这里整条线索都由拉丁语提供：mas 生出 masculus，masculus 经法语进入英语，之后才缩略成 male。

items.meaning: of the sex that does not give birth

definition_zh: 购物中心；林荫道；步行商业街
definition_en: a large shopping centre, originally a shaded walk or tree-lined promenade, and later a street given over to shops and pedestrians
core_image: 玻璃幕墙围起的长廊，两侧店铺灯火通明，人流沿中央通道向前
scene: 周末下午，自动门一开，冷气裹着爆米花的味道涌出来。On Saturday afternoon the mall was so crowded that we parked two blocks away.
sceneCN: 这里是「购物中心」（第 1 个义项：大型商场）；句意为周六下午商场挤得只能把车停在两个街区外。

pos.zh: 购物中心；林荫道；步行商业街

derivatives.zh: 由 mall 与 rat 复合，口语中指常年在商场闲逛的年轻人
由 mall 与 goer 复合，义为「常去商场的人」
由前缀 mega-（巨大）加 mall 构成，义为「超大型购物中心」

senses.title: A large enclosed shopping centre
senses.definition: a large building or covered area containing many shops, restaurants and places of entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 包含许多商店、餐厅和娱乐场所的大型建筑或有顶区域
senses.example: The new mall has a cinema and a food court on the top floor.
senses.exampleCN: 新商场顶层有电影院和美食广场。
senses.why: The long covered walk of the old game alley was rebuilt as a corridor of shops, so the promenade turned into a shopping centre.
senses.whyCN: 旧日球场那条有顶的长廊被改建成一条店铺走廊，散步的长道于是变成了购物中心。

senses.title: A tree-lined walk or promenade
senses.definition: a shaded walk or public promenade, especially one planted with trees
senses.definitionCN: 有遮阴的步道或公共散步场所，尤指两旁种树的
senses.example: Couples strolled along the mall in the afternoon shade.
senses.exampleCN: 午后树荫下，情侣们沿着林荫道散步。
senses.why: The name began with a long alley for a ball game, and any broad walk shaded by trees borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字最初指一条打槌球的长场地，后来任何有树荫的宽阔步道都借用了同一个词。

senses.title: A street set aside for pedestrians and shops
senses.definition: a street closed to traffic and lined with shops, common in American town centres
senses.definitionCN: 禁止车辆通行、两旁布满店铺的街道，常见于美国城镇中心
senses.example: The old main street became a mall after the cars were banned.
senses.exampleCN: 禁止汽车通行之后，那条老街变成了步行商业街。
senses.why: When a town closes a street to cars and hands it to shops, the old promenade sense widens into a business street.
senses.whyCN: 当一座城镇把街道对汽车关闭、交给店铺使用时，原本「散步长道」的词义就扩展成商业街道。

intro.en: Mall is usually traced through the game pall-mall, a long alley for ball and mallet, before it named a shaded walk and then a shopping centre.
intro.cn: mall 一般认为经由槌球游戏 pall-mall（用球与木槌、在长场地上进行的游戏）演变而来，先指有荫的长道，后指购物中心。

items.en: The route from the game to the modern word is reconstructed rather than documented, and dictionaries mark parts of it as uncertain.
items.cn: 从这种游戏到现代词义的路径多为重构，而非有明确文献记载，词典也把其中部分环节标为来源不确定。

items.en: Italian pallamaglio joined palla, a ball, with maglio, a mallet, and both words go back to Latin palla and malleus.
items.cn: 意大利语 pallamaglio 把表示球的 palla 与表示木槌的 maglio 组合起来，二者都可追溯到拉丁语 palla 与 malleus。

items.en: French took the game as pallemaille and passed the form to English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这项游戏称作 pallemaille，并在十七世纪把这个形式传给英语。

items.en: Pall-mall named both the game and the long alley where it was played, including the London walk that became The Mall.
items.cn: pall-mall 既指这项游戏，也指打球的长场地，其中包括后来称为 The Mall 的伦敦那条大道。

items.en: By the twentieth century mall meant a shaded walk and then, above all in North America, an enclosed shopping centre.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，mall 先指有荫的步道，随后尤其在北美指有顶的购物中心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the old game and on mall itself; the near-meaning group gathers words for shopping spaces and promenades.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在旧日游戏与 mall 本身之上的形式；近义组收表示购物场所与散步长道的词。

entries.definition: The old ball-and-mallet game and the alley where it was played.
entries.definitionCN: 旧日的球与木槌游戏，以及打球的长场地。

entries.definition: A young person who spends a lot of time in shopping malls.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间泡在商场里的年轻人。

entries.definition: An extremely large shopping mall.
entries.definitionCN: 超大型购物中心。

entries.definition: A tree-lined promenade in London, named after the old game alley.
entries.definitionCN: 伦敦的一条林荫大道，得名于旧日的球场长道。

entries.definition: A group of shops built together under one management.
entries.definitionCN: 集中建造、统一经营的一组商店。

entries.definition: A public square or a small group of shops around it.
entries.definitionCN: 公共广场，或其周围的一小片商店。

entries.definition: A covered passage with shops along both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧有店铺的有顶通道。

entries.definition: A broad public walk, especially one beside the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 宽阔的公共散步道，尤指海滨的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the name of a game alley, kept the shape of a long walk, and finally filled that shape with shops.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一条球场长道的名字，保留了长条形步道的形状，最后又在这个形状里填满店铺。

normal.en: Mall and pall-mall share one history: a ball, a mallet, and a long alley to play in.
normal.cn: mall 与 pall-mall 共用一段历史：一只球、一把木槌，还有一条打球的长场地。

normal.en: The Mall in London was a promenade before it was a name on a map, and the shopping sense came much later.
normal.cn: 伦敦的 The Mall 先是散步大道，后来才成为地图上的名字，购物义出现得更晚。

normal.en: Strip mall describes shops in a line beside a car park, the opposite of the enclosed mall.
normal.cn: strip mall 指停车场旁排成一线的店铺，与有顶的 mall 正好相反。

normal.en: Megamall simply adds mega, great, to mall, so the compound says the size twice.
normal.cn: megamall 只是把表示「巨大」的 mega 加到 mall 上，等于把尺寸说了两遍。

normal.en: Mall rat is informal for a young person who spends hours in a mall, built like bookworm and couch potato.
normal.cn: mall rat 是口语说法，指在商场里一待就是几小时的年轻人，构词方式类似 bookworm 与 couch potato。

abstract.en: A row of trees over a gravel path and a row of shop windows under one roof are the same long corridor, centuries apart.
abstract.cn: 碎石小径上的一排树，与同一屋顶下的一排橱窗，是同一条长廊，只是隔了几个世纪。

abstract.en: A ball game vanished, but the alley where it was played survives in the name of a shopping hall.
abstract.cn: 球戏消失了，但打球的那条长场地以购物大厅之名的形式留存下来。

abstract.en: The word lost its game, kept its shape, and filled the shape with shops.
abstract.cn: 这个词丢掉了游戏，保留了形状，又在这个形状里装满了店铺。

examples.en: The new mall has a cinema on the top floor.
examples.cn: 新商场顶层有一家电影院。

examples.en: Couples strolled along the mall in the afternoon shade.
examples.cn: 午后树荫下，情侣们沿着林荫道散步。

examples.en: The old main street became a mall after the cars were banned.
examples.cn: 禁止汽车通行之后，那条老街变成了步行商业街。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩尔」——摩尔商场里人潮涌动，走廊长得望不到头；记住 mall 是购物中心。

root: 一般认为源出意大利语 pallamaglio（球与木槌的游戏），经法语 pallemaille 进入英语作 pall-mall；词源路径多为重构，无可靠拉丁同族词直接对应。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a long shaded corridor for walking; the word then names a pedestrian shopping street and, finally, a large enclosed shopping centre.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一条有荫的狭长通道；词义由此指步行商业街，最后指有顶的大型购物中心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long glass-roofed corridor with shops on both sides and people walking down the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条玻璃顶的长廊，两侧是店铺，人流沿中央向前走。

branches.en: a glass door sliding open into cold air and bright lights
branches.cn: 玻璃门滑开，涌出冷气与灯光

branches.en: a row of trees over a gravel path
branches.cn: 碎石小径上的一排树

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin ball and mallet behind the Italian game, the French and English reshapings, and English compounds built on mall.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这里隔了两层留存：palla 给出「球」，malleus 给出「木槌」，共同构成英语接手的那项意大利游戏 pall-mall。

definition_zh: 管理；掌管；设法做到；勉力完成；应付；对付；靠有限的收入过日子
definition_en: to be in charge of a business or team, to succeed in doing something difficult, to deal with a hard person or situation, or to live on limited means
core_image: 一只手把缰绳一点点收短，躁动的马被稳稳按住
scene: 清晨的马场里，驯马师把缰绳一点点收短，躁动的马终于站定。By evening she was managing the whole stable on her own.
sceneCN: 这里 manage 是「管理、掌管」（第 1 个义项：对一批事务负起责任并决定它如何运转）；句意为到傍晚时，她一个人管着整座马房。图中可辨识物件：收短的缰绳、被按住的马、木栏与草料桶。

pos.zh: 管理；掌管；设法做到；应付；靠有限的钱维持

derivatives.zh: 由 manage 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「管理者；经理」
由 manage 加表示「行为、结果」的后缀 -ment 构成，义为「管理；管理层」
由 manage 加表示「可以……的」后缀 -able 构成，义为「可控制的；对付得了的」
由 manager 加 -ial 构成，义为「管理层的；经营上的」

senses.title: To be in charge of a business or team
senses.definition: to have responsibility for a company, a team or a set of affairs and decide how it should be run
senses.definitionCN: 对一家公司、一支团队或一批事务负起责任，并决定它该如何运转
senses.example: She manages a small team of six engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 她管理着一个由六名工程师组成的小团队。
senses.why: Italian maneggiare first meant to handle a horse with your hands, so the grip on the reins became the grip on a business: control is felt as something held, not merely ordered.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 maneggiare 最初指用手去摆弄、驯服一匹马，于是握住缰绳的那只手后来握住了事务：所谓控制，是被握住的感觉，而不只是发号施令。

senses.title: To succeed in doing something difficult
senses.definition: to succeed in doing something, especially when serious difficulties stand in the way
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在明显阻碍之下，仍然把某事做成
senses.example: He managed to finish the report before the power failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他赶在断电之前设法把报告写完了。
senses.why: A handler gets a stubborn animal to move by working it patiently, step after step; the word for handling therefore also means pushing a hard task through to the end.
senses.whyCN: 驯手对付一头犟牲口，是一步又一步耐心摆弄着让它动起来；所以「摆弄」这个词也用来表示把一件难事一路推到做成。

senses.title: To cope with a difficult person or situation
senses.definition: to deal with a difficult person, feeling or situation without losing control of it
senses.definitionCN: 面对难缠的人、情绪或局面，仍能不失控地应对下去
senses.example: She manages difficult customers without ever raising her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她应付难缠的顾客时从不提高嗓门。
senses.why: If managing is keeping a firm hand on something, a difficult customer is only one more thing that must be held steady instead of dropped.
senses.whyCN: 既然管理就是把一件东西稳稳握在手里，那么难缠的顾客也不过是另一件必须稳住、不能松手的东西。

senses.title: To live on limited money or time
senses.titleCN: 靠有限的收入过日子；精打细算
senses.definition: to live or keep going with only a small amount of money or time, using it carefully
senses.definitionCN: 在钱或时间很少的情况下，仔细盘算着维持下去
senses.example: The family manages on one small pension.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人靠一份微薄的养老金过日子。
senses.why: Running a household on little money is the same skill of handling resources, so manage also came to mean stretching whatever is already in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 用很少的钱撑起一个家，仍是同一套摆弄资源的本事，于是 manage 又表示把手里已经有的那点东西拉长来用。

intro.en: Manage reaches English through Italian and French, and the word still smells of the stable: to manage a horse came before managing a company.
intro.cn: manage 经意大利语与法语进入英语，词里至今还留着马房的气味：先会驯马，后来才谈管理公司。

items.en: Manus is the ordinary Latin noun for the hand, and the hand was the ancient image of control over any object.
items.cn: manus 是拉丁语中表示「手」的普通名词，而手一向是「掌控某物」的古老形象。

items.en: Italian kept the Latin noun as mano, still meaning hand, and built its verb of handling on that base.
items.cn: 意大利语把拉丁名词保留为 mano，仍指手，并在这个词基上造出了表示「摆弄」的动词。

items.en: Maneggiare meant to work something with the hands, above all to train and ride a horse in the riding school.
items.cn: maneggiare 意为用手去弄某样东西，其中最主要指在马术学校里驯马、驭马。

items.en: French manège named a riding school and the art taught there; its form and its stable sense pressed on the English borrowing of the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 manège 指马术学校以及在那里教的技艺；它的词形与马房义在十六世纪影响了英语的借入形式。

items.en: Modern English drops the stable and keeps the grip, managing ships, money, staff, crowds and finally a difficult afternoon.
items.cn: 现代英语丢掉了马房，只留下那只握住的手，用它来管船、管钱、管人、管人群，最后也管一个难熬的下午。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and words built on the Latin noun for hand; the near group gathers verbs for running, handling and coping.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及建立在拉丁语「手」这个名词上的词；近义组收表示经营、处理与应对的动词。
